bib.title: BERTopic: Neural topic modeling with a class-based TF-IDF procedure

question: Can topic modelling be done by clustering transformer document embeddings and describing clusters with a class-based TF-IDF, and does it match classical and clustering-based topic models?
hypothesis: Describing clusters with class-based TF-IDF rather than centroid proximity gives coherent topics that stay competitive across embedding models and datasets.
contributions: BERTopic: SBERT embeddings, UMAP reduction, HDBSCAN clustering, class-based TF-IDF topic representation
A dynamic topic modelling extension that reuses global IDF with per-timestep term frequencies, with optional smoothing
Comparison with LDA, NMF, CTM and Top2Vec on coherence, diversity and wall time

method.summary: Documents are embedded with a pre-trained SBERT model, reduced with UMAP, clustered with HDBSCAN (noise allowed), and each cluster is concatenated into one document and scored with c-TF-IDF to get topic words. Compared on three datasets by NPMI coherence and topic diversity, plus a dynamic-topic experiment and wall time.

datasets.name: 20 NewsGroups
datasets.preprocessing: removed punctuation, lemmatization, removed stopwords, removed documents with less than 5 words, lowercased

datasets.name: Trump's tweets
datasets.preprocessing: only slightly preprocessed; tokens lowercased. Binned to 10 timesteps for the dynamic experiment

datasets.name: UN general debates 2006-2015
datasets.preprocessing: binned to 9 timesteps; used for dynamic topic modelling only

other.embedders: Universal Sentence Encoder, Doc2Vec, all-MiniLM-L6-v2, all-mpnet-base-v2

other.note: HDBSCAN and UMAP parameters fixed between BERTopic and Top2Vec; values not given

models.name: LDA Sequence
models.architecture: original dynamic topic model (Blei and Lafferty, 2006)

inference.samples: 3 runs per topic count (10 to 50 topics in steps of 10), so 15 runs per score; dynamic: 3 runs at 50 topics over 9 timesteps, 27 values per score (Table 3 caption); Trump has 10 timesteps in section 5.1 but the caption says 9

parameters.c-TF-IDF: W_t,c = tf_t,c * log(1 + A / tf_t), A = average words per class
parameters.topic_reduction: iteratively merge least common topic with its most similar one to reach a user-specified number
parameters.dynamic: W_t,c,i = tf_t,c,i * log(1 + A / tf_t) with global IDF
parameters.smoothing: L1-normalize c-TF-IDF per topic and timestep, average t and t-1; optional (BERTopic-Evolve)

other.hardware: 2 cores Intel Xeon CPU @ 2.00GHz and one Tesla P100-PCIE-16GB GPU
other.wall_time_protocol: Trump data, 1000 to 43000 documents in steps of 2000 (read from Fig 1 caption)

metrics.name: Topic diversity (TD)
metrics.definition: percentage of unique words for all topics (Dieng et al., 2020), range [0,1]; 0 is redundant

metrics.name: Wall time
metrics.definition: seconds per topic model on Trump data, increasing document counts

eval.protocol: Means over 3 runs per topic count; no variance, seeds or significance test. Dynamic: NPMI at 50 topics per timestep, then averaged.

availability.data: OCTIS preprocessed datasets; Trump archive; UN debates csv (URLs in footnotes)

evidence.quote: The measure ranges from [-1, 1] where 1 indicates a perfect association.

limits: Coherence and diversity are proxies for a subjective judgement (5.3)
NPMI may not track human judgement for neural topic models (Hoyle et al., 2021) (5.3)
One topic per document is assumed; HDBSCAN probabilities are only a proxy for mixtures (7.2)
Topic words come from bags of words and can be redundant; maximal marginal relevance not explored (7.2)
Wall times measured with a GPU; will rise without one (6.4)
No variance or significance test; UMAP and HDBSCAN settings, noise share and topic-count effects not reported
Only one short-text dataset (Trump tweets), which is also the only lightly preprocessed one

terms.definition: all documents in a cluster concatenated into one class; weight is term frequency in the class times log(1 + average words per class / term frequency across classes)
